title: Definite integrals
competency: Find definite integrals by geometry and find anti-derivatives with the power rule.

keywords.def: The exact area under f from a to b: the limit of the Riemann sums.
A function F with F′(x) = f(x).
The set of all anti-derivatives, ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C.

en.text: If n grows without limit, Δx → 0 and the Riemann sums approach the exact area. That exact area is the definite integral ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx. For a straight-line graph you can get it from a triangle or trapezoid.

am.text: n ያለገደብ ሲያድግ Δx → 0 ይሆናል፤ የሪማን ድምሮች ትክክለኛውን ስፋት ይቀርባሉ። ይህ ስፋት ዴፊኒት ኢንቲግራል ነው።

screens.title: From sum to integral
screens.ask: For 3x² on [0, 5], left sums are 90 (5 strips) and 106.875 (10 strips). Right sums are 165 and 144.375. The exact area is about
screens.after:
Left sums are too small: 90, then 106.875.
Right sums are too big: 165, then 144.375.
The exact area is squeezed between them, and both close in on 125.
That limit is the definite integral: ∫ from 0 to 5 of 3x² dx = 125.

screens.title: Squeeze the area of 3x² on [0, 5]
screens.ask: Change the number of strips n. Watch both sums close in.

screens.title: Definite integral
paras: For f(x) ≥ 0 on [a, b], let n grow without limit (Δx → 0).
The exact area is ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx.
The sign ∫ is a long "s" for sum; Δx becomes dx.

screens.title: ∫ from 1 to 3 (x + 1) dx as a shape
screens.ask: Tap the points. The region under y = x + 1 from x = 1 to x = 3 is a trapezoid.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The exact area under f from a to b: the limit of the Riemann sums.

screens.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 0 to 2 (3x + 2) dx = ___
screens.why:
y = 3x + 2 is a straight line above the x-axis on [0, 2].
The region is a trapezoid.
Parallel sides: f(0) = 2 and f(2) = 8. Width 2.
Area = (1/2)(2 + 8)(2) = 10.
screens.clue: Draw the line; the region is a trapezoid.

screens.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 0 to 4 2x dx = ___
screens.why:
y = 2x starts at 0, so the region is a triangle.
Base 4, height f(4) = 8.
Area = (1/2)(4)(8) = 16.

screens.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 1 to 5 x dx = ___
screens.why:
The region from 1 to 5 is a trapezoid, not a triangle.
Parallel sides f(1) = 1 and f(5) = 5. Width 4.
Area = (1/2)(1 + 5)(4) = 12.
Trap: (1/2)(5)(5) = 12.5 starts the region at 0.

screens.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from −2 to 3 (x + 2) dx = ___
screens.why:
f(−2) = 0, so the line meets the axis at x = −2.
The region is a triangle: base 3 − (−2) = 5.
Height f(3) = 5.
Area = (1/2)(5)(5) = 12.5.

screens.ask: Definite integral of a constant: ∫ from 0 to 3 5 dx = ___
screens.why:
y = 5 is a horizontal line.
The region is a rectangle, 3 wide and 5 high.
Area = 3 × 5 = 15.

screens.ask: Missing upper limit: ∫ from 0 to k 2x dx = 49 with k > 0. Find k = ___
screens.why:
The region is a triangle: base k, height 2k.
Area = (1/2)(k)(2k) = k².
k² = 49, so k = 7 (k > 0).
Check: (1/2)(7)(14) = 49. ✓
screens.clue: Write the triangle area in terms of k.

en.text: Anti-differentiation undoes differentiation. All anti-derivatives of f differ by a constant, so ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C. Power rule: ∫ x^α dx = x^(α+1)/(α + 1) + C when α ≠ −1. Constants come out and sums split. Check every answer by differentiating.

am.text: ኢንቲግሬሽን ዴሪቫቲቭን ይገለብጣል። ∫ x^α dx = x^(α+1)/(α + 1) + C (α ≠ −1)። መልሱን በዴሪቫቲቭ እናረጋግጣለን።

screens.title: Many answers
screens.after:
(x²)′ = 2x, (x² + 5)′ = 2x, (x² − 3)′ = 2x.
The derivative of a constant is 0.
So every x² + C has derivative 2x.
That is why an indefinite integral ends with + C.

screens.title: Anti-derivative
paras: Finding f(x) from f′(x) is anti-differentiation, or integration.
The set of all anti-derivatives is the indefinite integral ∫ f(x) dx.
If F′(x) = f(x), then ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C. C is the constant of integration.

screens.title: Power rule for integrals
paras: ∫ kf dx = k∫ f dx, and ∫ (f ± g) dx = ∫ f dx ± ∫ g dx.
screens.note: Raise the power by 1, divide by the new power.

screens.title: Rules for integrals
screens.ask: Tap each rule for an example.
items: xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C for n ≠ −1. ∫ x⁴ dx = x⁵/5 + C.
k ∫ f(x) dx. ∫ 6x² dx = 6 × x³/3 = 2x³ + C.
∫ f dx ± ∫ g dx. Integrate term by term, one C at the end.
Not the power rule: −1 + 1 = 0. It is ln|x| + C.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A function F with F′(x) = f(x).
The set of all anti-derivatives, ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C.

screens.text: Power rule for integrals: ∫ x⁷ dx =
screens.why:
Raise the power by 1: 7 + 1 = 8.
Divide by the new power: x⁸/8.
Add the constant: x⁸/8 + C.
Check: (x⁸/8)′ = 8x⁷/8 = x⁷. ✓
Trap: 7x⁶ is the derivative, not the integral.

screens.text: Power rule with a negative power: ∫ x⁻⁴ dx =
screens.why:
New power: −4 + 1 = −3.
Divide by −3: x⁻³/(−3).
x⁻³ = 1/x³, so the answer is −1/(3x³) + C.
Trap: 1/(3x³) loses the minus sign; −4x⁻⁵ is the derivative.

screens.text: Power rule with a fraction power: ∫ x^(1/3) dx =
screens.why:
New power: 1/3 + 1 = 4/3.
Divide by 4/3, which means multiply by 3/4.
∫ x^(1/3) dx = (3/4)x^(4/3) + C.
Trap: (4/3)x^(4/3) multiplies instead of dividing.

∫ 3x² dx = 3 × x³/3 = x³.
∫ 2x dx = 2 × x²/2 = x².
∫ 5 dx = 5x.
So the answer is x³ − x² + 5x + C (one C at the end).
Check: (x³ − x² + 5x)′ = 3x² − 2x + 5. ✓

screens.text: Match each function with its anti-derivative.
screens.why:
x⁴: power 5, divide by 5 → x⁵/5.
4x³: 4 × x⁴/4 = x⁴.
x⁻²: power −1, divide by −1 → −1/x.
√x = x^(1/2): power 3/2, divide by 3/2 → (2/3)x^(3/2).
7: a constant integrates to 7x.
screens.clue: Check each pair by differentiating the right side.

screens.text: True or false? By the power rule, ∫ x⁻¹ dx = x⁰/0 + C
screens.why:
The power rule needs α ≠ −1.
For α = −1: α + 1 = 0, and we cannot divide by 0.
So the power rule fails here.
The right result is ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C. False.

screens.text: Anti-derivative with a starting value: F′(x) = 6x² + 2 and F(0) = 3. F(x) =
screens.why:
Integrate: ∫ (6x² + 2) dx = 6x³/3 + 2x + C = 2x³ + 2x + C.
Use F(0) = 3: 0 + 0 + C = 3, so C = 3.
F(x) = 2x³ + 2x + 3.
Trap: 6x³ forgets to divide by 3; 12x + 3 differentiates instead.
screens.clue: Integrate, then use F(0) to find C.

items.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 0 to 2 (2x + 1) dx = ___
items.why:
Trapezoid with parallel sides f(0) = 1 and f(2) = 5.
Width 2.
Area = (1/2)(1 + 5)(2) = 6.

items.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 0 to 4 2x dx = ___
Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 1 to 5 x dx = ___
items.why:
Trapezoid: sides f(1) = 1 and f(5) = 5, width 4.
Area = (1/2)(6)(4) = 12.

items.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from −2 to 3 (x + 2) dx = ___
items.why:
Triangle from x = −2 (where f = 0) to x = 3.
Base 5, height f(3) = 5.
Area = 25/2 = 12.5.

items.text: Power rule for integrals: ∫ x⁵ dx =
items.why:
5 + 1 = 6; divide by 6.
∫ x⁵ dx = x⁶/6 + C.
5x⁴ is the derivative.

items.text: Power rule with a negative fraction power: ∫ x^(−3/2) dx =
items.why:
New power: −3/2 + 1 = −1/2.
Divide by −1/2, which means multiply by −2.
−2x^(−1/2) = −2/√x.
Answer: −2/√x + C.

items.text: Power rule with a negative power: ∫ x⁻² dx =
items.why:
New power: −2 + 1 = −1.
Divide by −1: −x⁻¹.
Answer: −1/x + C.
Check: (−1/x)′ = 1/x² = x⁻². ✓

items.text: Power rule with a negative fraction power: ∫ x^(−3/5) dx =
items.why:
New power: −3/5 + 1 = 2/5.
Divide by 2/5, which means multiply by 5/2.
Answer: (5/2)x^(2/5) + C.

∫ k dx = kx + C.
So ∫ 99 dx = 99x + C.
Check: (99x)′ = 99. ✓

Take the 10 out: 10 ∫ x⁴ dx.
∫ x⁴ dx = x⁵/5.
10 × x⁵/5 = 2x⁵.
Answer: 2x⁵ + C.

items.text: Integrate term by term: ∫ (x² − x) dx =
items.why:
∫ x² dx = x³/3.
∫ x dx = x²/2.
Answer: x³/3 − x²/2 + C.

∫ x⁻² dx = −x⁻¹ = −1/x.
∫ 4x³ dx = 4 × x⁴/4 = x⁴.
√x = x^(1/2), so ∫ √x dx = x^(3/2)/(3/2) = (2/3)x^(3/2).
Answer: −1/x − x⁴ + (2/3)x^(3/2) + C.
Trap: (3/2)x^(3/2) multiplies by 3/2 instead of dividing.

test.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 0 to 3 4x dx = ___

test.text: Power rule for integrals: ∫ x³ dx =
test.why:
3 + 1 = 4; divide by 4.
Answer: x⁴/4 + C.
3x² is the derivative, not the integral.

∫ 6x dx = 6 × x²/2 = 3x².
∫ 1 dx = x.
Answer: 3x² + x + C.

test.ask: Definite integral as an area: ∫ from 2 to 4 (x + 1) dx = ___
test.why:
Trapezoid: parallel sides f(2) = 3 and f(4) = 5.
Width 2.
Area = (1/2)(3 + 5)(2) = 8.

test.text: Power rule with a negative power: ∫ 1/x³ dx =
test.why:
Write 1/x³ = x⁻³.
New power: −3 + 1 = −2. Divide by −2.
x⁻²/(−2) = −1/(2x²).
Answer: −1/(2x²) + C.

notes.text: Example 2 d (p.137): the book gives (5/2)x^(−1/3) + c; correct is −3x^(−1/3) + c (−4/3 + 1 = −1/3). Lessons use the corrected answer.
Exercise 2.25 c, ∫ (3/x) dx, needs ln|x|, which the unit has not taught; it is shown as a "power rule fails" true/false item.
p.133: "As the number of subdivisions dx = (b − a)/n increases" is garbled; n increases and dx decreases.

screens.text: Strip width for a Riemann sum: Δx for [0, 6] with 3 strips is
screens.why:
Δx = (b − a)/n.
(6 − 0)/3 = 2.
Trap: 3 is n, not the width.
